questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose this country taking into consideration the university reputation and quality of research. I always enjoyed the nordic countries and the cold weather so I decided that this country would be great for an Erasmus + internship.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy! The international mobility department from the University of Copenhagen were super helpful and solved any doubt I had regarding the documents and insurance that I needed for this abroad stay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The secretary from the department was the person in charge of making a batch so I could access the laboratory facilities and hospital building. Also the laboratory manager and all members from the department helped with anything that I needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university housing offered different accomodation options across the city. In my case, the dorm area I was staying consisted in 3 building: one with private housing ( most expensive), another with shared apartments and one with single rooms and shared kitchens ( cheapest). In my case, each building had common areas to work and hang out with friends, common kitchen, laundry room, recycling room and cleaning equipment.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I was living in a single room with shared kitchen. The kitchen was fully equipped with fridges, stoves, microwaves, ovens, tables, chairs and a TV. Addititionally, plates, pots, pans, cups, glasses.. was provided by the housing company. There was plenty of space to cook and some days we even organised common dinners to eat all together.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus is a bit more expensive than outside. It is very convenient to walk 7 minutes and be at the university so I didn't have to buy any transport ticket (  I moved everywhere by bike). There were supermarkets near and it was very accessible by public transport in case you needed to go to the centre. I would also suggest signing up in the university housing as soon as possible because they start offering housing to the students who have been cueing longer.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I didn't have to register for any courses because I was doing my master's thesis internship abroad. However, I had to do some courses about laboratory safety to be able to have a permit to work there. I had to fill up a form with my personal information and the name of the  department I was working in to get a batch. Besides that, the laboratory manager provided me with a laboratory tour and safety precautions rules.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The laboratory manager was in charge to make sure that everyone had their required documents ready. So after my arrival, she helped me signing up for the laboratory safety online courses and booking a time slot to get the working batch. Additionally, the secretary of the department also helped me with the paperwork.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't register for classes because I was working in a laboratory. The only documents that I needed for this Erasmus were the Erasmus contract and the insurance.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would suggest to make sure to keep an eye to the deadlines for the paperwork so it is submitted on time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did the second year of my master's programme abroad which consisted in a master's thesis of 60 credits ECTS. After a 9 month internship, I had to submit a 50-70 pages report and present it in front of a commite at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Although I didn't need to attend any classes, there were some seminars from the department I was working in that were very interesting. Once a week, there were lunch seminars were one member presented her/his most recent work. Another day there were Journal Clubs where we reviewed and discussed recent papers published in our research field.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Master's thesis 30 ECTS

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Master's thesis 30 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend doing the master's thesis abroad because it is a great opportunity to get to know how is research in another country and experience living abroad surrounded by a new culture.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy snow proof clothes and footwear because it snowed from November until mid-April.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I expected in this country. However, public transport was cheaper than I thought!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of associations at the university ranging from sports clubs, dance groups, hiking club to science student associations. A part from that, students were invited to conferences and congresses that took place at the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going for hikes outside of the main city you are staying in to get to know the area in a different way. Also, I joined student gatherings that took place in the dorm such as international dinners, where each of us cooked a meal from our own country.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Weekends are a great opportunity to visit the archipelago. So, we often took a boat to an island and spend the day walking around surrounded by nature. We also went bouldering, ice skating, hiking when there was nice weather. In case of rainy days, it was the perfect opportunity to cook and bake together with friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The country I visited was very near geographically to Denmark so I didn't encounter any differences. However, compared to my hometown, all the shops closed very early ( except for supermarkets) so you had to make sure to plan accordingly to avoid arriving to the shop and find it closed. At the same time, everyone spoke English fluently so communication was not a problem at all!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend joining facebook groups such as " students in _________ ( your Erasmus destination)" , or focused in your favourite hobbie " Hiking around ______ ( name of your Erasmus destination)". However, while living in a student dorm, you constantly meet new people so don't be afraid! If you are taking classes at the university, you will meet local students during the lectures so suggest going for a coffee or eating together to chat and get to know each other.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Compared to my home country, people here spoke and behaved more quietly. For instance, I am used to speaking in the phone while I am in the bus or metro back at home. However, in this country public transport was a very quite environment! Also back at home, I am used to having pocket money while in my Erasmus destination, everyone paid everywhere by card ( there were even places that did not accept cash).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The work-live balance and the relax way they live. Having fika (coffee breaks in the afternoon) helped us to recharge batteries for the rest of the day! They appreciate a lot and take care of nature, it is very admirable!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I'd tell them to enjoy this learning and life experience a lot! It was an honour having been able to participate in an Erasmus in this country. It is an unique and incredible way to start working in a laboratory in a foreign university. The quality of research at this institution is amazing and you learn so many techniques, how to be independent and plan your own experiments. Don't worry about not knowing their native language, they speak English like a native. However, I would totally recommend learning some basics before arriving so you can say " hello, goodbye, thank you". It is a great way to start learning their culture!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would also suggest to plan all your experiments accordingly and dedicate some time for data analysis and writing the thesis! This way you will avoid last-minute issues and stress before the submission deadline.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I feel I've learned so, so much!! It has reinforced the idea that I want to pursue a scientific career after my master's. Looking back, I feel so happy seeing all the techniques that I have learned, all the experiments that I've done. After a lot of hours of data analysis and writing, submitting and presenting the thesis were moments I will never forget!!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes some experiments don't go as planned and you don't understand why. However, after taking a little break, looking back at the protocols and speaking with your supervisor, you can find the mistakes and plan a new experiment! I learned not to be afraid of making mistakes, it is the way we learn!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
